\chapter{Introduction}

\section{Background}

A portable coordinate measuring arm (PCMA) is a handheld metrology instrument used to capture three-dimensional (3D) coordinates directly from a physical object, as shown in Figure~\ref{fig:portable-coordinate-measuring-machine-arm} \citep{Leussink:2024}.
\begin{figure}[H]
	\centering
	\includegraphics[width=0.6\linewidth]{../../../../../portable-coordinate-measuring-machine-arm}
	\caption{A portable coordinate measurement arm \citep{Leussink:2024}.}
	\label{fig:portable-coordinate-measuring-machine-arm}
\end{figure}
PCMAs offer adaptable measurement capabilities across various engineering applications, including dimensional analysis, computer-aided design (CAD) inspection, reverse engineering, etc. \citep{Ibaraki:2023}. However, a primary limitation of conventional PCMAs is the absence of a position-holding mechanism. This leaves the arm vulnerable to positional instability and structural deformation during measurement or upon accidental impact \citep{Cuesta:2015}. In addition to this, the instability complicates calibration procedures, which strictly require the arm to remain as still as possible throughout data acquisition \citep{Rim:2019}.

As a result, integrating the design of an effective position-holding mechanism into the arm's joint addresses these limitations while enhancing operational safety. Such a joint design improves the kinematic stability of the arm, eliminates positional drift, and reduces operator fatigue.

\section{Aim and Objectives}

The aim of this project is to implement a position-holding mechanism on a PCMA to eliminate positional drift, enhance kinematic stability, and reduce operator fatigue during measurement and calibration.

\noindent The objectives of the project are:
\begin{enumerate}
	\item To generalise the conventional Denavit-Hartenberg(D-H) model derived by Professor Schreve and Mr. Hall, with the purpose of error modelling \citep{Hall:2010}.
	\item To design, build and test key components of the joint to assess the joint design's mechanical feasibility.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Scope}

In the process of determining D-H parameters, user manuals and available schematics will be used for information extraction. For the purposes of the project, the narrower system of interest (NSoI) is identified as the PCMA joint and the wider system of interest (WSoI)\footnote{The NSoI is the system being designed and the WSoI includes the NSoI and the elements that the WSoI interacts with, \citep{Callister:2011}}, as the NSoI, a reliable power source, as well as the preceding and succeeding link connected to joint in a controlled testing environment, as seen in Figure~\ref{fig:system-context} below.

In addition to this, due to project timelines, physical implementation of the proposed design will be restricted to constructing critical subsystems necessary to validate the core mechanical, electrical, and software functionality.

\section{Motivation}

PCMAs are becoming more popular than traditional coordinate measuring machines (CMM) for in-line\footnote{In the context of PCMAs, "in-line" refers to performing quality inspections and measurements directly on the production shop floor, instead of a temperature-controlled quality laboratory, \citep{Leussink:2024}.} and on-site industrial measurement \citep{Leussink:2024}. They have broad applicability across multiple industries such as aerospace, automotive, and heavy manufacturing, where having a portable measurement instrument decreases handling time, production delays, and revision of work.

Despite their growing popularity, the PCMA's revolute joints must satisfy competing demands, including:
\begin{itemize}
	\item Tight run-out tolerances for spatial accuracy.
	\item Sufficient holding torque to keep the arm stationary when required.
	\item Internal cable routing.
\end{itemize}
This has proved difficult since no commercially available joint designs have been found to meet these demands.

Additionally, it has been established that angular position errors at each joint propagate through the kinematic chain, which affects end-effector's accuracy. This proves that joints have a measurable impact on the PCMA's accuracy \citep{Meagher:2016}. This project addresses the knowledge gap by deriving joint specifications from a generalised model based on an error model that was developed by a Stellenbosch Alumnus, Leon Hall \citep{Hall:2010}. This will produce a validated joint and testing methodology to support future PCMA development.

	\item Chapter 1 introduces the project background, aim and objectives, scope, and motivation for project.

	\item Chapter 4 discusses concept development for the joint, in which a final concept is chosen and refined.
